 Order

This petition is filed by the petitioner-wife under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for transferring the OS No.455/2022, pending on the file of the Principal Judge, Family Court,
Bangalore, to the Court of the Family Court, Ballari, for disposal in accordance with law.

2. The brief fact of the case are as under:
The allegations of the petitioner disclose that the petitioner and respondent belongs to Mohammedan community and their marriage was solemnized on 01.08.2021 at Hotel Pola Paradise, Cowlbazaar, Ballari.

It is also asserted that after the marriage,
the petitioner-wife joined the respondent-husband and later on, they started to ill-treat her and subjected her to ill-treatment.

It is further allegations of the petitioner that on 13.07.2022, the respondent-husband has left the petitioner in her parental house by assaulting her and refused to take her back which has compelled her to lodge a complaint.
The complaint was also registered in Ballari Woman PS in Crime no.160/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 341, 323, 504 and 506 r/w 34 of IPC.

She contended that in order to over come the complaint, the husband has subsequently filed OS no.485/2022 on the file of the Principal Judge,
Family Court, Bangalore,, seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
It is the contention of the petitioner-wife that the petition is filed only to counter blast her complaint and she was all along subjected to ill-treatment.
It is also asserted that she has no means to travel to Bangalore and hence, she has sought for transfer of the MC petition from Bangalore to Ballary, Family Court.
Hence, this petition.
3. The respondent-husband has appeared through his counsel and seriously objected for transfer.
4. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner and the learned counsel for respondent.
Perused the records.

sentences.text: 5. The learned counsel for petitioner contended that petitioner-wife was subjected to ill-treatment and they filed a complaint.
As counter blast, a petition for restitution of conjugal rights is filed which is an after thought story.

It is asserted that she is not in a position to travel to Bangalore and hence,
she sought for allowing the petition.

6. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent -husband would contend that the respondent is having aged parents and he is required to take care of his aged parents and he is not in a position to travel from Bangalore to Ballari to prosecute the matter.
Hence, it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.
7. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, it is evident that the marriage between the parties was solemnized on 01.08.2021 in Ballari.
The allegations further disclose that the petitioner and respondent leave together in Bangalore in the house of respondent-husband and led married life.
However, the wife asserts that she was subjected to ill-treatment all along and thereafter, she was left in her parental house which has compelled her to lodge a complaint.
All the reconciliation efforts went in vain.

The records disclose that she has lodged a complaint on 25.09.2022 before the Woman Police, Ballari and the complaint was registered in Crime No.160/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 341, 323, 504 and 506 r/w 34 of IPC.
The husband has filed the original suit in the month of December 2022 which is evident from the records produced.

Hence,
prima facie, it is evident that suit for restitution of conjugal rights was filed only to counter the complaint filed under Section 498A of IPC.
The petitioner is the wife and not in position to travel and she does not have any means.

8. Looking to these facts and circumstances, the petition needs to be allowed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

OS. No.485/2022, pending on the file of the the Principal Judge, Family Court,
Bangalore, is withdrawn and transferred to the Principal Judge, Family Court,
Ballari, for disposal in accordance with law.
Send the copy of this order to both the courts concerned for compliance.
